The 15 Most Woke Sci-Fi Movies of All Time, VirtueVigil Rankings 2026

15 most ideologically loaded sci-fi films ranked by woke score margin. VirtueVigil scores Poor Things, The Creator, Captain Marvel, Avatar, The Last Jedi, Dune: Part Two, and more. Know what Hollywood encoded in your favorite sci-fi.

Science fiction is the genre of ideas. It is supposed to ask "what if?" and let you sit with the question. The best sci-fi respects the audience enough to trust them with ambiguity. The worst sci-fi answers the question before you finish asking it. The 15 films on this list are not the worst -- some of them are brilliantly made -- but they are the ones where progressive ideology does not just inform the story. It is the entire project.

VirtueVigil has now scored 193 sci-fi films across every subgenre: space opera, cyberpunk, dystopian fiction, alien invasion, time travel, superhero-adjacent, and animated fantasy. Across that catalog, a clear pattern emerges. These are the films where Hollywood stopped speculating and started sermonizing. The films that took the genre's biggest asset -- its ability to imagine worlds different from our own -- and used it to argue that our world is broken in very specific ways, ways that happen to align with progressive politics.

Every entry links to the full VirtueVigil review with complete scoring methodology. The margin (tradScore minus wokeScore) reflects how thoroughly progressive ideology dominates the work. A -38 margin means the film's woke content overwhelms its traditional content by 38 points on our 100-point dual scale. These are not close calls. They are the films Hollywood made when it decided the future should have a political thesis. Know what you are about to watch.

STRONGLY WOKE

#1. Poor Things (2023)

Woke Score: 47 • Traditional Score: 9 • Verdict: STRONGLY WOKE • Margin: -38 WOKE

Yorgos Lanthimos won four Oscars for a film about a woman brought back to life with a baby's brain installed in her adult skull -- and the film's central argument is that this, somehow, is what female liberation looks like. Bella Baxter (Emma Stone) discovers sexuality, philosophy, and self-determination entirely unconstrained by the repressive Victorian world around her, and the baby brain is treated not as a bug but as the thesis. A grown woman in a state of infantilized consciousness engages in graphic, explicit sex -- first for pleasure, then professionally in a Paris brothel -- and the film frames all of this as empowerment. With a woke score of 47, Poor Things earns the highest woke score of any sci-fi-adjacent film VirtueVigil has ever scored, and the highest margin of any film in any genre. The craft is undeniable. The ideology is inescapable. If you watch this, know that you are watching an argument about female autonomy delivered through one of the most deliberately transgressive frameworks in recent cinema. The four Oscars tell you where Hollywood stands on that argument.

#2. The Creator (2023)

Woke Score: 35.88 • Traditional Score: 4.9 • Verdict: STRONGLY WOKE • Margin: -30.98 WOKE

Gareth Edwards made a genuinely beautiful film with a genuinely bad politics problem. The Creator is set in 2070, where the United States blames artificial intelligence for nuking Los Angeles and wages war against AI across "New Asia" -- a spiritual, Buddhist-coded civilization living peacefully with robots. The American military operates a giant orbital weapons platform called NOMAD that obliterates Asian cities from space, and the film's protagonist, a U.S. special forces soldier (John David Washington), discovers that the AI's ultimate weapon is a little girl. Shot on location across five Asian countries with stunning visual texture and a Hans Zimmer score, the film's craft is beyond reproach. Its politics are not: America is the villain, American military power is genocide, and the robot child is the moral center. With a traditional score of just 4.9, The Creator has almost no redemptive traditional content. It is an anti-American polemic dressed in some of the most beautiful sci-fi imagery of the decade. The beauty makes the politics travel further, which is exactly the point.

#3. Bugonia (2025)

Woke Score: 28.94 • Traditional Score: 8.48 • Verdict: STRONGLY WOKE • Margin: -20.46 WOKE

Yorgos Lanthimos appears on this list twice. Bugonia is a skillfully made, darkly funny, and ultimately nihilistic black comedy thriller that wraps a radical anti-capitalist, environmentalist manifesto inside a genre-bending alien conspiracy kidnapping story. Two conspiracy-obsessed men kidnap pharmaceutical CEO Michelle Fuller (Emma Stone), convinced she is an alien overlord from the Andromeda galaxy responsible for killing Earth's honeybees and engineering humanity's destruction through corporate poisoning. Stone shaved her head for the role and earned a Best Actress nomination. Jesse Plemons matches her beat for beat. The film's argument -- that corporate capitalism is literally destroying the planet, that pharmaceutical companies are poisoning us, and that the only rational response is paranoia -- is delivered with enough craft to make the medicine go down. The -20.46 margin reflects a film that knows exactly what it is arguing and does not pretend otherwise. Lanthimos makes ideological films. He is good at it. That is the problem.

WOKE

#4. Captain Marvel (2019)

Woke Score: 19.44 • Traditional Score: 3.25 • Verdict: WOKE • Margin: -16.19 WOKE

The MCU's most deliberately ideological film, and the filmmakers would not dispute this. Released on International Women's Day 2019, directed by a female co-director specifically because the studio wanted a woman behind the camera for their first female-led superhero film, scored by the first female MCU composer, and structured around a feminist empowerment narrative that makes its thesis explicit rather than implicit. Carol Danvers begins the film with her memories suppressed and a male authority figure (Jude Law) telling her she is not ready and that emotion is weakness. By the climax, she has reclaimed her memories, unleashed her emotions, and discovered that her suppressed power was not a limitation imposed by nature but a cage imposed by men. The traditional score of just 3.25 tells the story: there is almost nothing in this film that is not in service of its ideological project. Captain Marvel is not a superhero film with a feminist message. It is a feminist message with superhero action sequences attached.

#5. Strange World (2022)

Woke Score: 27.5 • Traditional Score: 12.32 • Verdict: WOKE • Margin: -15.18 WOKE

Disney spent $180 million on an animated film about a family of explorers who discover that their miracle energy source -- a plant called Pando -- is actually a parasitic infection killing the giant turtle-like creature their entire civilization lives on. It also features Disney's first openly gay animated lead character. It lost an estimated $197 million. The environmental metaphor is the structural backbone: Pando is fossil fuel, Avalonia is industrial civilization, the creature they live on is Earth, and the monsters trying to destroy Pando are actually the planet's immune system trying to save itself. This is not subtext. It is a giant flashing neon sign. With a woke score of 27.5 and a traditional score of 12.32, Strange World is the most expensive progressive sermon ever animated, and the box office is the market's honest verdict. Audiences, including families with children, recognized what Disney was selling and chose not to buy it. The $197 million loss is a number the industry should remember.

#6. Eternals (2021)

Woke Score: 19.74 • Traditional Score: 5.95 • Verdict: WOKE • Margin: -13.79 WOKE

The most ambitious and most divisive film in the Marvel Cinematic Universe -- and the first MCU film to fail with both critics and general audiences, earning a 47% on Rotten Tomatoes. Ten immortal beings were sent to Earth 7,000 years ago by the Celestial Arishem to protect humanity, but their true purpose is darker: they were sent to prepare Earth for the birth of a new Celestial, and that birth will destroy the planet. Directed by Chloe Zhao fresh off her Best Director Oscar, Eternals is Marvel's most deliberate diversity play: a deaf superhero, a gay superhero with an on-screen family, the MCU's first sex scene, and a cast spanning nearly every demographic category. The -13.79 margin reflects a film where the ideological project -- representation as an end in itself -- competes with the storytelling. When representation drives casting and character design rather than story, the product becomes about the casting decisions, not the characters. Audiences noticed. The 47% Rotten Tomatoes score is the market's honest verdict on a film that prioritized politics over execution.

#7. Avatar (2009)

Woke Score: 26.14 • Traditional Score: 13.6 • Verdict: WOKE • Margin: -12.54 WOKE

The highest-grossing film in the history of cinema made $2.9 billion arguing that the American military is a mercenary force that destroys indigenous cultures for profit, and that the correct moral response is to switch sides and fight alongside the natives against your own species. The visual achievement is genuinely extraordinary -- James Cameron spent twelve years developing the technology to create Pandora, and the world-building is meticulous. But the politics are not ambiguous: Jake Sully is a paralyzed Marine who arrives on Pandora to take over his dead brother's avatar contract, integrates with the Na'vi, and eventually leads them in armed insurrection against the human corporation that wants their land. The film's traditional score of 13.6 -- the highest of any film in the WOKE tier -- reflects the genuine redemptive elements of family, loyalty, and connection to nature that Cameron builds into the Na'vi society. But the anti-military, anti-corporate, anti-Western framework is the engine. The most-watched film in human history is an argument against Western civilization. That fact alone earns its place here.

#8. A Different Man (2024)

Woke Score: 18.52 • Traditional Score: 6.3 • Verdict: WOKE • Margin: -12.22 WOKE

A Different Man is a woke trap in the most literal sense: the film presents one narrative (awkward man learns confidence, gains friendship, attempts romance) and pivots into a completely different narrative (rejected man psychologically terrorizes his neighbor) while asking the audience to celebrate his transformation from sympathetic outsider to gaslighting abuser. Edward (Aaron Schimberg) is a severely disfigured man living in isolation who becomes obsessed with a new neighbor, a struggling artist. After a dramatic physical transformation, he is no longer the object of pity -- but the film's real argument is that male desire and romantic pursuit are inherently predatory, that the ugly man and the handsome man are the same predator in different packaging. The -12.22 margin reflects a film that disguises an ideological argument about male entitlement and toxic masculinity inside an indie character study about self-acceptance. The bait-and-switch is the method. The message is the point.

#9. Megalopolis (2024)

Woke Score: 20.83 • Traditional Score: 8.98 • Verdict: WOKE • Margin: -11.85 WOKE

Francis Ford Coppola spent 40 years and $120 million of his own money making a film that argues, without ambiguity or subtlety, that America is Rome at the end, that our institutions are corrupt and decadent, and that only visionary progressives willing to tear down the old and build something new can save us. Adam Driver's Cesar Catilina is an architect genius who can stop time and has invented a miraculous building material called Megalon. He wants to demolish New Rome and replace it with a utopia, and the film frames him as a persecuted visionary fighting against reactionary forces who cling to a dying system. The craft is real: Driver's performance is magnetic, the production design is extraordinary, and this is not the work of a filmmaker who has lost his abilities. It is the work of a filmmaker who has lost his audience. Megalopolis is a $120 million argument that progressive revolution is the only answer to systemic decay. It is more interesting as a cultural artifact than as a film. As a film, it is a sermon that forgot to build a congregation first.

#10. Star Wars: The Last Jedi (2017)

Woke Score: 20.58 • Traditional Score: 9.2 • Verdict: WOKE • Margin: -11.38 WOKE

Rian Johnson did not accidentally write a movie that deconstructed Star Wars mythology, humiliated its male heroes, and explicitly argued that the past must be destroyed. He did it on purpose, with full awareness, and has defended every choice since. The 42% audience score on Rotten Tomatoes is the market's honest verdict. The 91% critical score is the establishment's ideological endorsement. Poe Dameron, the franchise's most charismatic male hero, opens the film by winning a battle and losing a bombing fleet -- set up so female authority figures can spend the rest of the film punishing him for toxic masculinity. Vice Admiral Holdo, with a lavender pixie cut and a wardrobe from a Sundance cocktail party, refuses to share her plan, then sacrifices herself in a maneuver that had never been established as possible. Luke Skywalker, the hero of the original trilogy, is revealed as a bitter, failed recluse who considered murdering his nephew and needs a young woman to teach him hope again. The -11.38 margin reflects a film whose ideological project was to dismantle the franchise's traditional hero mythology and replace it with a progressive one. It succeeded at that specific goal, and the franchise has never recovered.

WOKE LEAN

#11. Borderlands (2024)

Woke Score: 17.5 • Traditional Score: 8.26 • Verdict: WOKE LEAN • Margin: -9.24 WOKE

Lionsgate spent $115 million turning a beloved M-rated video game into a PG-13 Guardians of the Galaxy knockoff. The result debuted at 0% on Rotten Tomatoes, earned a D+ CinemaScore, grossed $33 million, and lost the studio an estimated $80 million. The premise follows bounty hunter Lilith (Cate Blanchett) hired to retrieve a kidnapped girl on Pandora, only to discover the girl holds the key to an ancient alien vault. Borderlands is a woke-lean film more by default than design: the ideological elements (female-led action ensemble, anti-corporate villainy, found-family dynamics replacing traditional structures) are standard Hollywood template rather than deliberate argument. The -9.24 margin registers the default progressive framework that now comes baked into virtually every studio tentpole. Borderlands is not an ideological film in the way Poor Things or The Creator are. It is a creatively bankrupt one that happens to be ideologically progressive because that is what the template requires. The $80 million loss suggests audiences are tired of both.

#12. Avatar: Fire and Ash (2025)

Woke Score: 21.6 • Traditional Score: 13.4 • Verdict: WOKE LEAN • Margin: -8.2 WOKE

James Cameron has now made three Avatar films. Each one is technically extraordinary and ideologically predictable. Fire and Ash is both the best-looking film of 2025 and an almost proud repetition of every idea the franchise put on the table in 2009. The anti-military messaging, the noble-indigenous-vs.-corporate-colonizers framework, and the white protagonist who becomes the best version of the culture he joined: Cameron finds this territory comfortable, and he never leaves it. The plot takes Jake Sully and Neytiri into grief after the events of The Way of Water, introduces the fire-adapted Ash People led by Varang, and brings back Stephen Lang's Quaritch as the franchise's primary villain. David Thewlis joins as chief of the Wind Traders, a nomadic Na'vi faction. The traditional score of 13.4 -- the highest on this list -- reflects the genuine family and community values that Cameron weaves through the Na'vi culture. But the ideological framework is unchanged from 2009. Cameron has found his sermon and he is going to keep preaching it as long as audiences keep buying tickets. Given the franchise's track record, that will be a while.

#13. Dune: Part Two (2024)

Woke Score: 19.36 • Traditional Score: 11.55 • Verdict: WOKE LEAN • Margin: -7.81 WOKE

Denis Villeneuve accomplished something Hollywood rarely manages: he adapted one of science fiction's most complex novels with the seriousness it deserves, without dumbing it down for multiplex audiences. The Harkonnen scenes, shot in black-and-white under a black sun, are among the most striking images in recent blockbuster cinema. Austin Butler's Feyd-Rautha is genuinely unsettling. But conservative viewers should know: this is not an adventure about a hero's triumph. By deliberate design, Dune: Part Two is an anti-colonial, anti-messianic critique of the white savior narrative that Frank Herbert built into the novel's structure. Paul Atreides's rise is framed as a warning, not a victory. His Fremen holy war is a cautionary tale about charismatic leaders who exploit religious belief for political power. The -7.81 margin is relatively modest and the film earns its traditional content honestly -- the themes of family legacy, duty, and self-sacrifice are real. Dune: Part Two is a great film. It is also an ideologically coherent one, and knowing what Villeneuve is arguing makes you a better viewer, not a worse one.

#14. The Matrix Resurrections (2021)

Woke Score: 15.05 • Traditional Score: 8.75 • Verdict: WOKE LEAN • Margin: -6.3 WOKE

A fascinating failure: it fails as a blockbuster sequel, it fails as an action film, it partially fails as a story, and yet it succeeds as a piece of cinema that forces genuine engagement. Neo has been resurrected inside a new Matrix, working as a video game designer whose signature title is a trilogy called The Matrix. Trinity lives nearby as a married suburban woman named Tiffany who does not recognize him. The machines rebuilt both of them because their love generates more power than either alone. Lana Wachowski made this film as a direct response to Warner Bros. threatening to make a Matrix sequel without her, and the meta-textual commentary -- about being forced to resurrect a franchise you already finished, about corporate control of art, about the commodification of revolutionary ideas -- is the most interesting thing in it. The -6.3 margin is driven more by this anti-corporate, creator-as-oppressed-victim framework than by the gender politics of the original trilogy. Resurrections is a deeply personal film that happens to have a political thesis. Its failure at the box office ($157 million on a $190 million budget) suggests audiences wanted a Matrix sequel. They got a Wachowski manifesto instead.

#15. Mickey 17 (2025)

Woke Score: 11 • Traditional Score: 5 • Verdict: WOKE LEAN • Margin: -6 WOKE

Let's dispense with the pretense: Mickey 17 is a Trump allegory. Bong Joon-ho has confirmed it publicly. The villain, Kenneth Marshall, is a populist politician who delivers speeches about making the colony great, wears distinctive fashion that reads as a visual joke on Trump, plans genocide against indigenous alien creatures, and is played by Mark Ruffalo, one of Hollywood's most vocally progressive activists. This is not coded or subtext. It is the text. Robert Pattinson gives one of the year's most entertaining performances as Mickey, an "expendable" cloned worker who dies repeatedly and is reprinted, and Bong's technical gifts make the film work as entertainment even when its politics are aimed directly at conservative viewers. That is either a tribute to its craft or a warning about how effective entertainment can be as an ideological delivery system. With a woke score of 11 and a traditional score of just 5, the -6 margin reflects a film that is more political cartoon than nuanced argument. The question for viewers is whether the craft justifies the caricature.

The Takeaway

Five observations emerge when you look at these 15 films together.

First, the three STRONGLY WOKE films share a common thread: they are all good films. Poor Things won four Oscars. The Creator is visually stunning. Bugonia earned Emma Stone an Oscar nomination. This is not a list of failures. It is a list of films where the ideology and the craft are mutually reinforcing -- the better the film, the more effectively the ideology travels. A bad film with a progressive message is easy to dismiss. A great film with a progressive message is much harder. These three films are the ones where Hollywood's progressive politics are delivered with the most skill. That makes them the most effective, not the least dangerous.

Second, the WOKE tier -- Captain Marvel through The Last Jedi -- is where the industry's default progressive template becomes fully visible. These are franchise films, blockbusters, and would-be tentpoles built on the assumption that audiences want feminism, environmentalism, diversity-as-product, and anti-Western critique baked into their entertainment. The box office results suggest otherwise: Strange World lost $197 million, Eternals was the MCU's first critical and audience failure, and The Last Jedi fractured the Star Wars fanbase in ways the franchise has never healed. Captain Marvel made money, but the sequel cratered. These are the films where Hollywood learned -- or should have learned -- that audiences can tell when ideology drives the bus.

Third, the WOKE LEAN tier is the most interesting because several of these films are genuinely good. Dune: Part Two is a masterpiece that happens to carry an anti-colonial thesis. The Matrix Resurrections is a deeply personal film that wears its politics on its sleeve. Avatar: Fire and Ash is more of the same from Cameron, but "more of the same" from the highest-grossing director in history is not nothing. Mickey 17 is a Trump allegory that is also genuinely entertaining. These films prove that ideology in sci-fi is a spectrum, not a binary. Some films have an argument. Some arguments have a film. The difference matters.

Fourth, the absence of certain films is worth noting. Blade Runner 2049, Arrival, Interstellar, Inception, The Martian, Edge of Tomorrow -- these are major sci-fi films of the last decade that score firmly traditional or balanced. Sci-fi is not uniformly woke. The genre is vast and varied. For every Poor Things there is an Interstellar. For every Captain Marvel there is an Edge of Tomorrow. The data supports this: of the 193 sci-fi films VirtueVigil has scored, these 15 are the most ideologically loaded. Browse all scored sci-fi at VirtueVigil.com to find the films that match your values.

Fifth, and most important for parents: science fiction is the genre kids use to make sense of the future. It shapes how they think about technology, authority, family, and what it means to be human. When your teenager comes home from the multiplex buzzing about the latest sci-fi blockbuster, ask which one. Then look it up. These scores tell you not just whether a film is visually impressive or narratively satisfying, but what it believes -- and what it wants your child to believe, too. The space battles are the delivery system. The ideology is the payload. Know what is in the cargo hold before your kids climb aboard.
